sources.source: Statistics Sweden (SCB), average monthly salary after sector, all sectors, total gender.
sources.unit: SEK/month; annual comparator calculated as monthly × 12
sources.definition: SCB average monthly salary across all sectors, both sexes (total gender), for each year 1992–2025. Salary is not disposable income or actual annual earnings.
sources.transformation: Annual comparator is monthly average multiplied by 12; nominal values. Monthly source values retained in the separate salary file.

sources.source: Sveriges Riksbank, Historical Monetary and Financial Statistics for Sweden, Volume I, Svante Prado workbook, Tables I.A10.1 and I.A10.2.
sources.definition: Hourly earnings by manufacturing industry category and sex, plus a separately identified source-provided weighted average. Source table categories are represented in Swedish in the CSV.
sources.coverage: Sweden; manufacturing workers. Coverage varies by industry and sex. Male categories are observed from 1860 or later depending on category; female coverage starts between 1865 and 1952 by category. Male weighted average 1871–2013; female weighted average 1921–2013.
sources.transformation: Transcribed source observations without annualization or interpolation. Missing cells are omitted. This sectoral hourly series is not directly equivalent to all-sector monthly salary; overlap does not imply equivalent population or method.

sources.source: FZ.se's 2017 summary of Swedish new console prices, based on Cuponation's compilation from historical Swedish articles and forums including FZ, Aftonbladet and Sweclockers.
sources.unit: nominal SEK per console/package at reported Swedish launch
sources.definition: Reported Swedish new retail price at launch for Nintendo console models; discrete product launch observations, not calendar-year average retail prices. Switch 2 has no fixed official Swedish price; the recorded point is the console-only retail price reported at launch.
sources.coverage: Sweden; nine observations: NES (reported as 1987, although Swedish retail availability began 1 September 1986), SNES 1992, Nintendo 64 1997, GameCube 2002, Wii 2006, Wii U Basic and Premium 2012, Switch 2017, and Switch 2 2025. The NES year/launch price are uncertain and marked; its displayed wage share uses the 1987 male weighted-average manufacturing hourly wage annualized at 2,080 hours, not the all-sector SCB salary series. Wii U is split into two launch packages per contemporary Swedish reporting. Wii is approximate; FZ reported about 2,700 SEK including VAT and one game on release day. Switch 2's 6,795 SEK is a reported Swedish retailer price for the console-only package; Swedish retailers set prices independently. FZ/Cuponation's 2017 compilation is secondary; see per-row source_url and price_basis in the data file.
sources.transformation: Nominal reported Swedish launch prices transcribed from the cited sources. The Wii price is approximate and includes one game; Wii U Basic/Premium are separate packages. Switch 2 uses a contemporaneously reported retailer console-only price, not an official fixed Swedish price. For 1992 onward, wage share is launch price ÷ SCB all-sector average monthly salary for that year ÷ 12 × 100. For the NES source-year 1987 only, wage share is launch price ÷ male weighted-average manufacturing hourly wage from the Riksbank historical series ÷ 2,080 (40 hours × 52 weeks) × 100. That point uses a different population and is not directly comparable to SCB points. No inflation adjustment, no year-to-year trend arrow between distinct models.

data.price_basis: FZ/Cuponation reports this price/year; Swedish retail availability began in 1986, so exact launch year and launch price are uncertain
data.wage_basis: 1987 male weighted average manufacturing hourly wage × 2,080 hours (40 × 52); not comparable to the all-sector SCB salary series
